originating_session_goal: Determine whether any governance products or frameworks are equivalent, similar, overlapping, or adjacent to the StegVerse SPE and commit-time admissibility governance framework.
core_question: May this proposed transition bind consequence now, at the commit boundary, using reconstructable current standing rather than historical approval alone?

classes.definition: Attempts to decide or gate action from evidence, policy, state, or consequence before execution.
Shares runtime decision, policy, authorization, or enforcement behavior.
Supplies required evidence, provenance, identity, risk, or governance input to SPE.
Governs surrounding management, lifecycle, assurance, compliance, or documentation context.
Valuable but answers a different governance question.

frameworks.name: DecisionAssure-style causal-continuity trace review
frameworks.relationship_summary: Tests whether a supplied trace can support authority reconstruction and causal-continuity claims.
frameworks.boundary: Candidate interoperability target; does not become authority.

frameworks.name: CARE Runtime-style public runtime-governance platform
frameworks.relationship_summary: Runtime-governance and consequence-boundary language relevant to StegVerse.
frameworks.boundary: Source status remains bounded by available public evidence; no equivalence claim.

frameworks.name: Open Policy Agent / Rego
frameworks.relationship_summary: Runtime policy-decision engine over structured input.
frameworks.boundary: Policy decision is not full admissibility, authority, evidence, custody, and standing reconstruction.

frameworks.name: Cedar Policy
frameworks.relationship_summary: Authorization policy semantics and permit/forbid decisions.
frameworks.boundary: Strong authorization overlap, but not a full transition admissibility framework by itself.

frameworks.name: XACML / ABAC / PBAC policy engines
frameworks.boundary: Primarily access authorization, not transition admissibility or continuity reconstruction.

frameworks.name: Zanzibar / OpenFGA relationship authorization
frameworks.boundary: Answers who can access what, not whether a proposed consequence-binding transition is admissible now.

frameworks.name: Runtime governance for AI agents
frameworks.relationship_summary: Checks next actions, paths, policies, or operating constraints.
frameworks.boundary: Must still prove evidence, authority, delegation, and standing at commit.

frameworks.name: Policy Cards
frameworks.relationship_summary: Machine-readable policy artifact and runtime obligations.
frameworks.boundary: Can feed SPE policy references; does not itself prove standing.

frameworks.name: Guardrails AI / NeMo Guardrails / Llama Guard
frameworks.relationship_summary: Runtime output, action, and model-behavior constraints.
frameworks.boundary: Safety constraints are not a full admissibility proof engine.

frameworks.name: in-toto
frameworks.relationship_summary: Supply-chain layout, steps, and signed provenance.
frameworks.boundary: Strong evidence-chain input; does not decide transition admissibility.

frameworks.name: SLSA
frameworks.relationship_summary: Supply-chain assurance levels and provenance requirements.
frameworks.boundary: Assurance input only unless bound to SPE standing rules.

frameworks.name: Sigstore
frameworks.relationship_summary: Signing, transparency log, and artifact identity evidence.
frameworks.boundary: Cryptographic evidence input, not governance authority.

frameworks.name: W3C Verifiable Credentials / DID / OpenID Connect / OAuth2
frameworks.relationship_summary: Identity, claims, delegation, and access-token ecosystems.
frameworks.boundary: Can represent identity and delegation evidence; token validity is not full admissibility.

frameworks.name: SPIFFE / SPIRE
frameworks.boundary: Strong identity and workload-standing input; not transition governance alone.

frameworks.name: OSCAL
frameworks.boundary: Compliance and control evidence input, not commit-time execution authority.

frameworks.name: NIST AI RMF
frameworks.relationship_summary: AI risk management lifecycle and trustworthiness framing.
frameworks.boundary: Management framework, not a commit-time execution gate.

frameworks.name: ISO/IEC 42001
frameworks.boundary: Organizational governance system, not SPE-equivalent standing reconstruction.

frameworks.name: EU AI Act
frameworks.boundary: External legal duties can constrain SPE, but do not implement SPE.
